Rugged tablet for Agility CMMS/EAM and the AgilityMobile app

Agility is a cloud-based CMMS and EAM platform from SSG Insight, a maintenance software company with its UK office in Wakefield. SSG Insight says it has worked in asset maintenance software since 1983 and it joined Aptean on 21 August 2024. Its named UK customers include Bakkavor (13 sites, about 2,300 work orders a week), boohoo, West Midlands Metro, Keolis Amey Metrolink, NHS Borders and The Sheffield College. The main system runs in a browser. AgilityMobile is the companion app for engineers and technicians, and it requires a connection to an Agility 9 system, so this page is for teams that already run Agility and now need devices for the people doing the work.

On the floor, technicians use AgilityMobile to accept, suspend and complete work orders, fill in compliance checklists, capture fault codes, attach photos and documents, raise reactive requests, book out spare parts and scan asset QR codes to pull up work orders. That work happens in plant rooms, depots, food factories and tram sheds, where a consumer tablet with an exposed glass front, no 4G and a small battery is the wrong tool.

This page sets out what SSG Insight publishes about the app's requirements, which of the three Tuga devices fits those requirements and why, how to get the app running, and what we cannot confirm from the vendor's published material. We sell the hardware only. Agility licensing and configuration come from SSG Insight.

Requirements

What Agility CMMS/EAM and the AgilityMobile app needs from a device

Each item below comes from SSG Insight, part of Aptean's own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Android app from Google Play

    AgilityMobile is published on Google Play as 'Agility' by SSG Insight Ltd (package com.ssginsight.agility), version 2.2.3, updated 23 April 2026. The listing's 'Requires Android' value could not be confirmed when this page was written, so check the About this app section on Google Play on your own device before ordering in volume. The same app is on the Apple App Store with a minimum of iOS 16.0, but we sell Android and Windows devices only. Source: play.google.com

  • A licensed Agility 9 system

    The Google Play description opens with 'REQUIRES A CONNECTION TO AN AGILITY9 SYSTEM. If you do not have a main Agility system contact SSG Insight to request a demo.' The app is of no use on its own; the tablet is a client for your existing Agility system. Source: play.google.com

  • Offline working

    The App Store listing for the same app (version 2.2.3, bundle com.ssginsight.agility) lists 'Process jobs and raise new ones while offline' among its features, and SSG Insight's light rail page says passenger feedback can be gathered on mobile devices 'whether on or offline'. The Google Play description does not repeat the offline statement, so confirm the behaviour on your own Agility system before relying on it in areas with no signal. Source: apps.apple.com

  • In-app QR code and barcode scanning

    SSG Insight's facilities management page says AgilityMobile users can 'scan asset QR codes to see work orders in seconds'. App Store release notes refer to a barcode reader on route sheet pages and to its handling when a user has denied camera permissions, which points to camera-based scanning. The vendor publishes no scanner hardware requirement. Source: ssginsight.com

  • Camera and storage for attachments

    The AgilityMobile product page lists attaching images and documents to work orders, viewing asset repair history, manuals and diagrams, and completing compliance checklists. A usable rear camera and enough storage for manuals and photos matter in practice, although the vendor publishes no camera or storage figure. Source: ssginsight.com

  • Network connection for a cloud-hosted system and push notifications

    Agility is offered cloud-hosted (Guernsey Water moved to the hosted version in 2020) and the AgilityMobile product page lists push notifications when new jobs arrive or a job status changes. Technicians moving between buildings or sites need Wi-Fi and, where Wi-Fi is patchy, mobile data. Source: ssginsight.com

  • Windows devices get the browser-based main system only

    SSG Insight describes the main Agility system as browser-based: 'As a browser-based system, Agility can be securely accessed from any computer.' We found no Windows or Microsoft Store version of AgilityMobile, and no supported-browser list or Windows hardware requirement is published. A Windows tablet therefore runs the Agility web application in a browser and does not get the app's offline mode. Source: ssginsight.com

The W10 is not a device for AgilityMobile, because SSG Insight publishes no Windows version of the app. It is the pick where you want the browser-based Agility system on a rugged tablet, for example a supervisor allocating jobs and running dashboards from a workshop, a stores desk booking parts, or a fixed point on a line where a wired Ethernet connection and an HDMI output are useful. It runs Windows 11 Pro with a full desktop browser, so it accesses Agility the same way an office PC does, but without the app's offline mode.

  • Browser-based main Agility system, accessible 'from any computer': Windows 11 Pro on an Intel N100 up to 3.4GHz with 8GB RAM and 128GB storage, running a full desktop browser.
  • Workshop and stores use: 100Mbps RJ45 Ethernet, HDMI for a larger screen, USB-A and USB-C, and a pogo pin dock connector for the £49.99 charging dock.
  • Mobile use where needed: dual-band Wi-Fi 5, Bluetooth 5.2 and optional 4G LTE, with a 10.1 inch 1280 x 800 multi-touch display and a removable 5000mAh battery.
  • Protection: IP65, dust tight and protected against water jets, but not rated for immersion, so it is for dry and splash areas rather than wash-down.
Get a business quote Full specification
Worth knowing. Three honest caveats. First, the Google Play listing's minimum Android version could not be verified when this page was written, so we do not quote one; check 'Requires Android' in About this app on Google Play before ordering. The Tuga A10 runs Android 14 and the A6 runs Android 15. Second, SSG Insight publishes nothing about NFC or RFID tag reading in AgilityMobile, so we make no claim that the NFC on the A10, A6 or W10, or the optional UHF RFID reader on the W10, does anything with Agility. Third, there is no Windows version of AgilityMobile that we could find, so the W10 only gives browser access to the main Agility system and does not get the app's offline working; if your technicians need offline mode, buy the A10 or A6. SSG Insight also publishes no recommended devices or screen-size guidance, and the scanning described on its site is in-app, with no dedicated scanner requirement, so the A10 having no scan engine is not a known gap. The A6 does have a Zebra 2D scan engine, but we cannot confirm that AgilityMobile accepts its input, so treat it as a bonus to test rather than a reason to buy.
Setting up

Getting Agility CMMS/EAM and the AgilityMobile app running

  1. Confirm with your Agility administrator or SSG Insight that your organisation runs an Agility 9 system with mobile licensing, and that each technician has a user account. The app requires a connection to an Agility 9 system and does nothing without one.
  2. On the Tuga A10 or A6, sign in to Google Play with your organisation's Google account or a managed device account, search for 'Agility' by SSG Insight Ltd and install it. While on the listing, check the 'Requires Android' figure under About this app; the A10 runs Android 14 and the A6 Android 15.
  3. Open the app and sign in with the system details and user account your Agility administrator gives you. Grant the camera permission when Android asks so in-app QR code scanning and photo attachments work.
  4. Ask your Agility administrator or SSG Insight how offline working is configured on your system, then test it on one unit by completing a job with Wi-Fi and mobile data switched off and reconnecting afterwards, before you issue devices to the team.
  5. Fit the hand strap supplied in the A10 box, apply a tempered glass screen protector, and if the device lives in a van or on a maintenance cart, fit the vehicle mounting dock. For shared devices, add a charging dock at the workshop or handover point.
  6. Order a single trial unit first. We welcome one-unit trials before a fleet order, and multi-unit discounts apply automatically from two units when you place the main order.

Agility CMMS/EAM and the AgilityMobile app on a Tuga device

AgilityMobile is published on Google Play as 'Agility' by SSG Insight Ltd, version 2.2.3 as of April 2026, and the Tuga A10 runs Android 14. The listing's minimum Android version could not be confirmed from the listing page when we wrote this, so check 'Requires Android' under About this app before a fleet order. The app requires a connection to an Agility 9 system, so you need an existing Agility licence. Tuga Hardware has no certification or testing arrangement with SSG Insight; we are stating the published requirement and the device's operating system.

SSG Insight's App Store listing for the same app (bundle com.ssginsight.agility, version 2.2.3) lists 'Process jobs and raise new ones while offline', and its light rail page refers to gathering passenger feedback on mobile devices whether on or offline. The Google Play description does not repeat this, so test it on your own system during a trial. The offline statement applies to the app, which runs on Android, so it concerns the A10 and A6. The W10 runs the browser-based main system only and does not get the app's offline mode.
